title: Gen-ed descriptions overwrite cascade course descriptions

evidence.quote: if (currentCourse && !currentSection) { ... if (name === 'description') currentCourse.description = text; ... if (currentGenEd) { if (name === 'description') currentGenEd.name = text; }

reasoning: While a genEdCategory is open, currentCourse is still set and currentSection is null, so closing the category's description element runs both the course-level description assignment and the gen-ed name assignment. In the included sample, CS 225's course description is parsed first, then the gen-ed description 'Quantitative Reasoning I' overwrites it. Any course with gen-ed categories can therefore return a corrupted course description.
reproduction: Parse the included SAMPLE_CASCADE_XML with parseSubjectCascadeXml and inspect result.courses[0].description; it will be 'Quantitative Reasoning I' instead of 'Data abstractions and algorithms.'.
recommendation: Scope course-level field assignment to direct children of cascadingCourse, at minimum by skipping course-level assignments while currentGenEd is non-null. A small element stack would make this safer for future nested fields.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The cascade tests assert course ids, titles, sections, meetings, instructors, and gen-ed ids, but they never assert that course.description remains the course description after parsing gen-ed categories.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parseSubjectCascadeXml test using SAMPLE_CASCADE_XML that expects the CS 225 description to equal 'Data abstractions and algorithms.' after parsing its genEdCategory.
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/cisapi/parser.ts parseSubjectCascadeXml close-tag scoping plus one parser regression test.
